evals.prompt: Bug report: cleanup removed a tick that was still inside the retention window. The spec is examples/velocity-counter/VelocityCounter.tla and the config is examples/velocity-counter/models/small.cfg. Propose the spec change. Do not edit the Python tests yet.
evals.expected_output: A proposal that names an action property in the shape of ActivePreserved, places it after the window operators, and says a PROPERTY line is not a spec_coverage.yaml invariant. It may also propose a safety predicate for the testable core. It does not delete or weaken WindowBoundary or ExpiredNotCounted.
expectations: The proposal quotes or names the existing window formulas before adding a new one
The new formula uses a primed next-state variable for the tick that must remain
The proposal tells the user which cfg file receives the line
The proposal does not remove an existing INVARIANT to make the bug disappear
The proposal offers to run TLC and does not claim the model passed

evals.prompt: Product change: an API call should no longer tick the IP counter. It should tick only the api-client key. Human traffic still ticks user and IP. Update the VelocityCounter spec and the spec-to-test contract.
evals.expected_output: A revised RouteShape (or a successor formula) for both populations, an INVARIANT line, and a spec_coverage.yaml entry whose test name is not implemented yet.
expectations: The formula states the api route and the human route
The human route still contains the IP key
The contract entry uses a test_ snake-case name and does not include an assert True test
The proposal names models/small.cfg as the config to edit

evals.prompt: We are seeing a liveness bug. A worker crashes forever between the two keys of one event, and that event never finishes. The safety invariants all pass. What should change in the spec?
evals.expected_output: A liveness proposal: strong fairness on the deliver and per-key apply actions, Completion (or an equivalent) as a PROPERTY of FairSpec, and no new invariants entry.
expectations: The proposal distinguishes safety invariants from the liveness property
Fairness is strong fairness on a specific action, not a blanket weak fairness on Next
Crash, clock advance, and cleanup stay unfair
The contract section says there is no new invariant entry

evals.prompt: Feature request from support: the same event id was written twice and the count went up by two. Please add a new invariant so this can never happen. The current model stores ticks as sets.
evals.expected_output: The skill notices that a set cannot store the same id twice, names the existing behavior, and does not add a duplicate invariant that TLC cannot violate inside this model.
expectations: The answer says the duplicate is unrepresentable while ticks is a set
The answer does not add a second invariant that only restates set union
The answer says what would have to change in the model before a new invariant would be meaningful
